simple.meaning: מֶלֶךְ (Melek) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with kingship and in connection with prophetic witness.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in 1 Chronicles, Jeremiah, beginning at 1 Chronicles 8:35. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, kingship, prophetic witness.

simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows מֶלֶךְ through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.

The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
The king commanded Jerahmeel the king’s son, and Seraiah the son of Azriel, and Shelemiah the son of Abdeel, to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet; but Yahweh hid them.

Then they took Jeremiah and threw him into the dungeon of Malchijah the king’s son, that was in the court of the guard. They let down Jeremiah with cords. In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire.

definitions.full: H4429. Melek II. מֶ֫לֶךְ proper name, masculine son of Micah, a Benjamite (on ׳מ as individual name see Gray Prop. N. 116, 122 n. 4 ; compare Phoenician proper name מלך (see Bloch); Sabean proper name מלכם CIS iv. 1 ; Palmyrene proper name מלכו Vog Palm. 92 and others Nabataean id. , Eut Nab 21, 4 and others Vog Nab 1, 2 ); — 1Chr 8:35 ( ᵐ5 Μελχηλ ), 9:41 ( ᵐ5 Μαλαχ ; ᵐ5 L Μελχιηλ in both). מֶ֫לֶךְ 178 noun masculine king (general Semitic; see Biblical Hebrew); — ׳מ absolute Dan 2:10 2 t.; construct 4:34 6 t.; usually emphatic מַלְכָּא Ezra 4:8 154t., ָ ה Dan 2:11 ; plural מַלְכִין Ezra 4:15 9 t., ִ ים 4:13 (Hebraism, BeRy M 41 *); emphatic מַלְכַיָּא Dan 2:44 2 t.; — king 2:4-5 , 132t. Daniel; Ezra 4:8 , 11 42t. Ezra ( מַלְכַיָּא מֶלָךְ of Nebuchadnezzar Dan 2:37 , of Artaxerxes Ezra 7:12 [compare Cooke 71.3, of Xerxes ]; מַלְכִין Dan 7:17 +? מַלְכוּ 7:23 ).
